topics.topic: Choose whether generated owner-delivery routes handle authentication, parsing, and direct photo_delivery delegation or call deliverer_api route handlers
questions: Does the scan route call an API handler that validates and delegates, or does the generated router call deliverer_api.check_token and deliverer_api.parse_project_id and then call photo_delivery.scan_project_photos itself?
Who reads and validates the delivery body and who calls photo_delivery.deliver_project_photo: an API route handler or the generated router using deliverer_api.check_token and parse_project_id?

Does the mark route delegate to an API handler, or does the generated router call check_token, read PublishedRequest including photo_id, call parse_project_id and then call photo_delivery.mark_photo_published itself?
Should the owner flow depend on API route handlers, or on generated router routes that use API helper capabilities and delegate directly to photo_delivery?

Does the scan route call a deliverer_api handler that delegates to photo_delivery, or does the generated router call check_token and parse_project_id and then call photo_delivery.scan_project_photos directly?

Does the delivery route call a deliverer_api handler, or does the generated router read DeliverRequest, call check_token and parse_project_id, and then call photo_delivery.deliver_project_photo directly?

Does the mark route call a deliverer_api handler, or does the generated router read PublishedRequest, validate the token, project id and photo_id form, and call photo_delivery.mark_photo_published directly?
For the owner flow, are the route handlers in deliverer_api or are they generated table routes in deliverer_router that use deliverer_api utilities and delegate directly to photo_delivery?

Do the generated routes call `photo_delivery` directly after calling the authentication and parsing helpers of `deliverer_api`, or do they call unnamed route handlers owned by `deliverer_api` that perform the checks and delegation?

quotes:
`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend` generates with its `fastapi_sync_v2` backend, and it
holds only what that backend emits. It serves every route as a table route: the body of a delivery and of a mark
is read as = models.DeliverRequest and = models.PublishedRequest, the token is compared by `check_token` of
`deliverer_api` before the body is read, the project id is judged by its `parse_project_id`, and the route
then calls one operation of `photo_delivery`.

The calling agent is outside this service and organises the work (R0-15). It reads and publishes in the Portal with
its own session. It reaches the deliverer only through the routes of `module:deliverer_router`, whose handlers in
`module:deliverer_api` check the token and delegate to `module:photo_delivery`. The deliverer never calls the Portal. Showing a photo to the client is a later
action of the owner in the Portal and is not part of this flow.
judgement.why: State 3 makes each generated router route call photo_delivery directly after using deliverer_api helpers, while State 4 assigns the handlers and delegation to deliverer_api.

topics.topic: Decide whether check_token, parse_project_id, and refusal_answer are public deliverer_api capabilities callable by deliverer_router
questions: Are check_token, parse_project_id and refusal_answer public capabilities of deliverer_api that flow steps and later contracts may name, despite their omission from its Candidate public capabilities?
Are `check_token`, `parse_project_id` and `refusal_answer` public capabilities of `module:deliverer_api` that `module:deliverer_router` may call, or does `deliverer_api` expose only `answer_health`?

quotes:
Written on 2026-11-18 from the accepted States 0 to 4. These are the operations another module or the boundary of the
service may call. Inputs and outputs name their meaning, and the exact signatures are decided in State 6. The test
`test_each_module_offers_exactly_its_public_operations` of `prototypes/portal_deliverer/test_deliverer.py` fails when a
module of the prototype offers any other public function.

None until the surface is served. The health route answers through `public_op:deliverer_api.answer_health`
without a token. Every other route checks the token with `module:deliverer_api` before it reads the body, reads
the body of a delivery or a mark by its request model, judges the project id with `module:deliverer_api`, calls one
operation of `module:photo_delivery`, and answers every refusal through `module:deliverer_api`.
judgement.why: State 5 defines the exact public-operation set and distinguishes the sole deliverer_api public operation from the deliverer_api helpers used inside generated routes.

topics.topic: Map every service termination path to its ServiceExit value and process exit status, and assign the observing capability
questions: For every way run_service ends, which ServiceExit member does it choose and which status from EXIT_STATUSES becomes the process exit status?
Which capability observes the listening boundary and every terminating event, selects ServiceExit, and applies the corresponding EXIT_STATUSES status?

quotes: The exit status of the process: the status of the row of the imported `EXIT_STATUSES` constant for the member of = models.ServiceExit that A8 gives the way the process ends: START_FAILED before it listens, SERVED when a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops its web server after it has begun listening, and SERVER_FAILED for any other end after that. A failure is reported on the standard error stream; the text of that report is not part of the contract.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns observation and classification to deliverer_service.run_service and maps every termination class through EXIT_STATUSES.

topics.topic: Assign responsibility for detecting malformed delivery and publication request bodies and invoking refusal_answer
questions: When the delivery body has the wrong form, does the router or framework catch that defect and call deliverer_api.refusal_answer, or does deliverer_api itself read and refuse the body?
Who detects and routes a malformed PublishedRequest or photo_id to refusal_answer: the generated router or deliverer_api?

quotes:
`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend` generates with its `fastapi_sync_v2` backend, and it
holds only what that backend emits. It serves every route as a table route: the body of a delivery and of a mark
is read as = models.DeliverRequest and = models.PublishedRequest, the token is compared by `check_token` of
`deliverer_api` before the body is read, the project id is judged by its `parse_project_id`, and the route
then calls one operation of `photo_delivery`. `AuthenticationRequired`, every `DelivererError` and a request whose
body or form the framework refuses are each answered by `refusal_answer` of `deliverer_api`, so every refusal
leaves as M08 (A5 rules 1, 9 and 10). `deliverer_api` therefore cannot import the router back.
